decisions.reason: After two years the low-pile decorative carpet still costs little to keep in the collection, and a sibling design (C) was already pruned, which leaves A as one of the surviving variants whose value may still materialize.
The hand-knotted wool silk carpet reinforces the craftsmanship positioning, and as a made-to-order showpiece it costs little to keep while project demand remains uncertain.
The corner bench extends the established upholstery and dining offer for residential and hospitality projects, so holding the option further is justified at low cost.
The low-pile carpet adds little keeping cost within a broad portfolio, but with several similar carpet options held, it is a moderate pruning candidate if results stay weak.
The multi-model swivel shell chair line represents a larger committed investment serving contract and residential markets, and it is worth keeping while demand resolves.
